- Applies when: A product whose value depends on importing or connecting data (orders, domains, users) before anything useful appears.
- Exceptions: Products where a wrong default causes irreversible or billed actions (sending to customers, charging money) may need one extra confirm step before the first such action. Evidence is a settings audit log, not the wizard screens (which were not observable); the interval from setup to the first imported record was not in evidence, so the minute count is indicative only.
- Do: Step 1: confirm pickup address. Step 2: connect your store (one authorise button). Done: orders start arriving; a link says 'Adjust packaging, labels and notifications in Settings'.
- Don't: A nine-step wizard covering branding, notification copy, packaging rules and label layout before the first order can be imported.
- Check (static): Count the steps and required fields in the first-run flow spec. Each one must be justified as blocking first value; any step for a preference that has a default is a violation. Check that a pointer to settings for further tuning exists on the completion screen.
- Check (live): With a fresh test account, time from first login to the first real record (imported order, connected domain) appearing in the main list. Count the screens passed. Confirm every skipped preference has a working default in settings.

### ONB-003 — Guided setup at first access, framed by goal

**Rule:** Offer new accounts a guided setup at first access, as a short wizard or a list of setup tasks named by the user's goal, each showing progress and a start action.

- Why: A newcomer does not know the product's vocabulary; tasks named by outcome and showing how much is left let them pick a goal and see the end of the effort.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify documented, dhl documented, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: First access to a new account, or first visit to a product area that needs configuration before it does anything.
- Exceptions: A product whose provisioning already leaves the account working may skip the task list and land straight on the work queue. The task-list form with progress and time estimate was observed in one portal, on a product-area overview rather than the account home; the others document a wizard or setup tasks without showing their screens, so goal naming and progress rest on that one portal.
- Do: Overview card 'What would you like to do next?' with tasks 'Replace my VPN - 0 of 3 complete - about 15 min - Get started' and 'Filter DNS traffic - 0 of 1 complete - about 5 min - Get started'.
- Don't: A setup list named after internal modules ('Configure Gateway', 'Configure Tunnel') with no progress and no time estimate.
- Check (static): Check the first-access landing spec has a setup block. Each task label must name an outcome in user terms, not a module name, and show a progress count (n of m) and a start link to the first incomplete step.
- Check (live): Log in with a fresh test account and confirm the setup block appears without searching for it. Complete one step and return: the progress count must have increased and the start link must point to the next incomplete step.

### ONB-004 — Retire setup prompts once setup is done

**Rule:** Remove setup tasks and first-run banners from the landing page once their steps are complete, and keep a way to reopen them from help or settings.

- Why: A finished checklist is noise on the most visited page; the landing area should switch to daily work once the account works.
- Confidence: low (source inferred; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The landing page or an area overview shows setup tasks, a wizard entry or a first-run banner.
- Exceptions: Required actions with risk (for example enabling two-step authentication, or open work tasks) stay until done and are not dismissible. No portal shows the retirement itself: all three reference accounts were already set up and showed no checklist on the landing page, which is consistent with removal but could also mean dismissal or that none was ever shown; one portal only records a 'show onboarding wizard' flag at account creation, with its later value unknown, and no reopen entry was seen anywhere.
- Do: After the last setup step, the landing page shows the work queue and KPIs; Help menu keeps 'Restart setup guide'.
- Don't: A '5 of 5 complete' checklist still pinned at the top of the home page months later.
- Check (static): Check the landing-page logic hides the setup block when all tasks are complete (or dismissed) and that a reopen entry exists in help or settings.
- Check (live): Complete every setup task on a test account, reload the landing page and confirm the setup block is gone. Find and use the reopen entry; the setup block must come back with all tasks shown as complete.

### ONB-005 — Start setup inside the normal shell with a few path cards

**Rule:** When setup has more than one starting path, open it as a page inside the normal navigation shell with two to four choice cards, each with a one-line consequence, instead of a separate full-screen flow.

- Why: Keeping the sidebar and help visible lets people leave and come back, and choice cards with consequences let them pick the right path without knowing the jargon.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Adding a main object that can be created in different ways (connect existing, transfer, buy or create new).
- Exceptions: A single-path setup needs no choice step. Whether later steps stay inside the shell was not observed; only the first step was.
- Do: Page 'Add a site' with cards 'Connect a domain - make your site faster and more secure', 'Transfer a domain - save on renewals', 'Buy a domain - register a new one', sidebar still visible.
- Don't: A full-screen modal with no navigation and a dropdown 'Method: [Zone setup / Registrar transfer / Registration]'.
- Check (static): Check the first setup route renders inside the main layout (sidebar and top bar present) and offers 2-4 cards, each with a title and a one-line description of the outcome.
- Check (live): Start the add flow from the list page's primary action. Confirm the sidebar is still visible, each card has a description, and leaving through the sidebar and returning lands on the same choice page.

### ONB-006 — Connect the data source in one authorise step, then sync automatically

**Rule:** Make connecting the user's main data source a single authorise action that returns to the product, asks only the mapping questions it cannot infer, offers a connection test on the same screen, and starts automatic sync by default.

- Why: First value usually means the user's own records appearing; every manual mapping or import step between authorise and the first record delays it.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The product's core data lives in another system the user already runs (a store, an identity provider, a code host).
- Exceptions: When the mapping cannot be inferred (several locations, several accounts), ask one picker question right after authorising. In the reference account the location was a user pick from a lookup list, and the other import options are current values not proven defaults; only auto-import on by default is proven. Connecting an integration was not observed from scratch in the other two portals.
- Do: Button 'Authorise store' opens the store's consent page; on return, one picker asks which location to import from, 'Import orders automatically (about every 20 minutes)' is already on, and a 'Test connection' button sits beside 'Authorise'.
- Don't: After authorising, an empty mapping form for 15 fields and an 'Import now' button the user must remember to press.
- Check (static): Check the connect flow has exactly one external authorise step, returns to the product, asks no mapping question whose answer is the only valid option, sets automatic sync on by default, and exposes a test-connection action on the same screen as the authorise action.
- Check (live): Connect a test data source from a fresh account. Count clicks and questions between 'Connect' and the first imported record. Confirm auto-sync is on without touching it and that the test action reports success or a specific error.

### ONB-007 — Onboard each feature in its own empty state

**Rule:** When a feature has nothing set up yet, use its empty state to onboard: say what it does, offer one primary start action, and add ready-made templates or code samples for the common jobs.

- Why: Most features are first met long after account setup; an empty state that starts the job in one click is the cheapest onboarding there is and needs no separate tour.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Any list or feature page that is empty because the user has not created anything yet (rules, automations, campaigns, API tokens, gateways).
- Exceptions: Empty because of filters or search is a different state: say no results match and offer to clear filters, not to create. A locked or paid feature shown as an empty upsell must say it is locked.
- Do: Heading 'Start automating your workflow', one line on what rules do, button 'Add new', and quick-setup buttons 'Assign service by destination country', 'Require signature over a set value'.
- Don't: An empty table with 'No rules found.' and no action, or a blank page with only the page title.
- Check (static): For every list or feature page, check the zero-items branch renders a heading that explains the feature, one primary create action, and (for configurable automation) at least one template or sample. Check the filtered-empty branch has separate copy.
- Check (live): On a fresh test account open each main list and feature page. Each must show an explanation and a start action; pick a template where offered and confirm it opens a prefilled form.

### ONB-008 — Make onboarding prompts dismissible and non-blocking

**Rule:** Show promotional or optional onboarding (feature intros, agent setup, new-feature cards) as dismissible cards or pills inside the page, never as blocking steps, and keep them dismissed once closed.

- Why: Optional prompts that cannot be closed train people to ignore the whole area; a dismiss control respects users who already know the feature.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Prompts for optional features, upsells, tours or integrations shown on home or area overviews.
- Exceptions: Required actions (open work items, a security step such as two-step authentication) stay visible until done and are not dismissible.
- Do: Card 'Run your marketing on autopilot' with 'Get started' and a 'Dismiss' button; a pill 'Onboard your coding agent' above the home heading with a 'Don't show this again' control.
- Don't: A modal on every login offering a feature tour, closable only by finishing it.
- Check (static): List every onboarding card, pill and banner. Each optional one must have a labelled dismiss control and a persisted dismissed flag per user; required-action items must be listed as such.
- Check (live): Dismiss each optional prompt, reload and log in again: it must stay hidden. Confirm required-action banners have no dismiss control.

### ONB-009 — Introduce redesigned areas once, with a replayable tour

**Rule:** When an area changes substantially, show a one-time welcome dialog listing the few changes with a single 'Got it' close, and keep a 'Tour' button on the page to replay it.

- Why: Returning users lose their bearings after a redesign; a short once-only summary orients them, and a replay button serves those who closed it too fast.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: A redesigned page or navigation that existing users already knew in its old form.
- Exceptions: Small changes need no dialog; a changelog link is enough. Never chain the welcome dialog into a multi-step blocking tour. The welcome dialog and the tour buttons were observed on different pages of one portal, and that portal documents a replayable tour for its redesigned navigation; the once-only behaviour was not tested.
- Do: Dialog 'Welcome to the new records view' with four headed items (Customize columns, Pin records, Nameserver settings, one more record type), a Close button and 'Got it'; the page header keeps a 'Take a tour' button.
- Don't: A ten-step coach-mark tour that starts automatically on every visit and cannot be replayed once skipped.
- Check (static): Check the welcome dialog is gated by a per-user seen flag, lists at most about five changes, has both close and confirm actions, and that the page header has a replay entry.
- Check (live): Open the redesigned page with a test user who has not seen it: the dialog appears once. Close it, reload: it does not reappear. Use the tour button and confirm it replays.

## integrations

### INT-001 — One list of connected integrations

**Rule:** Give connected integrations one list page that shows every connection as a row with its name, the account or resource it is linked to, and row actions to open its settings or remove it.

- Why: People need one place to answer 'what is connected to this account' before they change, debug or remove anything; a scattered set of connections cannot be audited.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The product connects to at least one external system (store platform, carrier, identity provider, file transfer, webhook target).
- Exceptions: A product with exactly one fixed, non-removable connection may show it as a card on its settings page instead of a table. Very large catalogs of connections of one kind may be split per product area, but each area still gets its own list.
- Do: Integrations page: search box, table with columns Integration / Linked account / Actions (Settings, Remove), and an 'Add integration' action above the table.
- Don't: Connections found only by opening several unrelated settings pages, with no page that lists them together.
- Check (static): Find the integrations list page in the route map or spec. Confirm it renders one row per connection, each row shows a name and the linked account or resource, and each row exposes an open-settings action and a remove action (inline or in a row menu).
- Check (live): Connect two test integrations, open the integrations page, and confirm both appear as separate rows with name, linked account, and working open-settings and remove actions.

### INT-002 — Adding starts from a catalog of providers

**Rule:** Make 'Add integration' open a catalog of available providers, each tile or row leading to that provider's own setup form.

- Why: Each provider needs different credentials and options; choosing the provider first keeps every setup form short and specific.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl documented, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: More than one provider or connection type can be added.
- Exceptions: When the catalog lives in an external marketplace, the add action may link out, but it must say so (external link icon or text) and return the user to the integrations list after installation.
- Do: 'Add an identity provider' opens a grid of provider tiles with a 'Back to integrations' link; each tile opens a form only for that provider.
- Don't: One generic 'New connection' form with a provider dropdown at the top that reshapes twenty fields depending on the choice.
- Check (static): Trace the 'Add' action on the integrations list. It must route to a catalog view listing providers, and each provider entry must route to a provider-specific setup page or dialog. If the catalog is external, the link must be marked as external.
- Check (live): Click 'Add integration', confirm a catalog of providers appears with a way back to the list, pick one provider and confirm the form shows only that provider's fields.

### INT-003 — Each integration has its own detail page

**Rule:** Give each connected integration its own detail page that holds all of its configuration, its log and its maintenance tools, reached from its row in the list.

- Why: All decisions about one connection are made while looking at that connection; spreading them across global settings hides which connection an option belongs to.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: An integration has more than a single on/off option.
- Exceptions: Options shared by every integration (for example a global auto-import schedule) may stay on the integrations list page, above or below the table. A connection with its own day-to-day user interface may instead get its own navigation group with its own 'Settings' item (see INT-011).
- Do: Detail page with a breadcrumb Settings > Integrations > Provider, H1 with the provider name, and tabs Settings / Field mapping / Logs / Tools.
- Don't: Per-connection options placed on a global settings page behind a 'Choose integration' dropdown.
- Check (static): For each integration type, confirm one route renders its detail page with a breadcrumb back to the list, and that no global settings page needs an integration picker before its fields can be edited.
- Check (live): From the integrations list, open one row's settings; confirm the URL identifies that connection, the breadcrumb returns to the list, and configuration, logs and tools for that connection are all reachable on that page.

### INT-004 — Test the connection on the spot

**Rule:** Put a 'Test connection' action next to the credentials of every connection, available right after the connection is saved or authorized, and show a pass or fail result that names the cause without discarding the form.

- Why: A connection that saves without error can still fail at the first real sync; testing at setup time turns a silent failure hours later into an immediate, fixable message.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The connection uses credentials, an authorization step, a host or an endpoint that can be wrong or expire.
- Exceptions: Integrations installed and authorized entirely by the other platform, with no credentials the user can edit, may rely on the status indicator (INT-005) instead of a test action.
- Do: Numbered setup steps ending with 'Authorize, then click Test connection'; the Test button sits beside Save and shows 'Connected: 3 orders found' or 'Failed: authentication rejected' under the form.
- Don't: Only a Save button, with the first sign of a wrong password being an empty order list the next day.
- Check (static): On every connection form or connection row, find a test action. Confirm it is enabled once saved values exist, calls a real connectivity check, and shows success or the provider's error message without clearing the form values.
- Check (live): Save a connection with a deliberately wrong test credential, click the test action, and confirm a specific failure message appears without leaving the page; fix the credential, test again, and confirm success.

### INT-005 — Visible status per connection

**Rule:** Show each connection's current status (for example Connected, Needs attention, Disconnected) as a status label in the list row and on the detail page, with a status filter when the list can grow long.

- Why: Without a status at the list level, a broken connection is found only by reading logs, so failures go unnoticed until downstream work stops.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Connections run continuously or on a schedule, so they can break after setup.
- Exceptions: Two reference portals show no connection status label in their integration lists; one relies only on a run log with an error column, which works only when the log is one click away and every run is listed. Prefer a status label anyway.
- Do: Connections table with a Status column ('Healthy', 'Needs attention') and a 'Filter by status' select; detail page header strip: Status, last successful sync, uptime.
- Don't: A list that shows only the provider name and linked account while the last ten syncs have failed.
- Check (static): Confirm the list row and the detail header both render a status value derived from the connection's last run or heartbeat, with distinct text (not color only) for each state. If the list paginates, confirm a status filter exists.
- Check (live): Break a test connection (revoke its token or stop its endpoint), wait for the next sync or heartbeat, and confirm the list and detail page both change to a failure status in text.

### INT-006 — Sync log beside the integration

**Rule:** Put a log of recent sync runs on the integration's own page, with time, duration, items processed, run type and error, plus a link to the full log and a way to look up why one record did or did not sync.

- Why: Self-service troubleshooting needs the evidence next to the settings that caused it; a log hidden elsewhere sends people to support for questions the data already answers.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The integration imports, exports or syncs data, or runs jobs on a schedule.
- Exceptions: Real-time connections with no discrete runs (for example a tunnel or a login provider) may show a live event log instead of a run table. The per-record lookup was observed in one portal only; skip it when records are not identifiable by the user.
- Do: Detail page tab 'Logs': timezone note, Refresh, table Time / Duration / Imported / Type (auto or manual) / Error for the last 10 runs, 'View all logs' link; a search by record number that shows the outcome reason, such as 'skipped: no items found'.
- Don't: A single global log page with no filter by integration, and no link to it from the integration.
- Check (static): On the integration detail page, find a log tab or section whose rows include timestamp, outcome and error text, and confirm it links to the full log pre-filtered to this integration. Confirm read-only log tabs do not show a Save bar.
- Check (live): Trigger one sync on a test connection, open its detail page, and confirm the new run appears in the log with time and outcome; follow 'View all logs' and confirm the full log opens filtered to the same integration.

### INT-007 — Surface sync failures outside the log

**Rule:** When a connection fails or becomes incompatible, show a page-level warning on the integrations pages that names the connection, the impact and the fix, and let people subscribe to alerts for status changes.

- Why: Errors that exist only as a cell in a log are found by people who already suspect a problem; everyone else learns about them from missing orders or locked-out users.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: A connection can fail or degrade without any user action (expired token, provider API change, remote outage).
- Exceptions: Transient single-run errors that the next scheduled run recovers from may stay in the log only; escalate after repeated failures.
- Do: Warning banner: 'Store connection is not compatible with the new shipping model. It may stop working on 1 July. Learn more.' and a 'Configure alerts' card on the detail page linking to alert settings for this connection's status changes.
- Don't: One failed run among fifty rows in a log table, with no banner, badge, email or alert.
- Check (static): Find the code path that handles a failed or incompatible connection state. Confirm it renders a page-level banner with the connection name, consequence and an action, and that the detail page links to an alert or notification setup for status changes.
- Check (live): Force a test connection into a failed state across several runs; reload the integrations list and detail page and confirm a warning banner appears with a next step; open the alert link and confirm it pre-selects this connection.

### INT-008 — Field mapping as an explicit list with defaults

**Rule:** Show which data the integration reads and writes as an explicit mapping list of labeled checkboxes and selects, pre-set to sensible defaults, with write-back to the other system as its own clearly labeled option.

- Why: Users must know which of their fields cross the boundary and in which direction; an explicit list with defaults lets most people accept it as is and lets the rest change one field.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The integration copies records or fields between systems (orders, products, customers, tracking numbers).
- Exceptions: Authentication-only integrations (login providers) exchange identity, not records, and need no mapping list.
- Do: Card 'Field mapping': 'Import order tags' [x], 'Import variant names' [x], 'Map order notes to' [Delivery instructions v]; card 'Write-back': 'Send tracking numbers back to the store' [x] with a sentence saying when it happens.
- Don't: Hard-coded, undocumented mapping, or a write-back that is on with no visible option and no explanation.
- Check (static): On the integration detail page, confirm a mapping section lists each imported or exported field with a control and a default value, and that write-back to the remote system is a separate labeled control whose helper text says when it runs.
- Check (live): Open a new test integration without changing anything, confirm the mapping options show pre-set defaults, untick one mapped field, save, run a sync, and confirm that field is no longer imported.

### INT-009 — Run-now and maintenance actions act immediately

**Rule:** Place run-now and maintenance actions (Import now, Refresh, Clear cache, Rotate token) as buttons in their own card or tools tab that act immediately, separate from the configuration form and its Save bar.

- Why: Mixing one-off jobs into a Save form makes people unsure whether clicking Save also runs the job, or whether the job uses unsaved values.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: An integration offers manual sync, re-import, cache reset, credential rotation or similar one-off jobs.
- Exceptions: A test-connection action may sit beside Save on the credentials form (see INT-004), because it checks the values being saved.
- Do: 'Tools' tab with cards: 'Manual import' (days field + Import now), 'Product cache' (Clear product cache), each card with one sentence explaining its effect.
- Don't: An 'Import all orders now' checkbox inside the settings form that runs only when the user clicks Save.
- Check (static): List every one-off job an integration offers. Confirm each is a button outside the Save-bar form, with its own helper text, and that it does not depend on unsaved form state.
- Check (live): Edit a field without saving, click a run-now action, and confirm the job runs immediately with feedback (toast or log row) and that the unsaved edit is neither saved nor lost silently.

### INT-010 — Credentials masked, rotation explained

**Rule:** Show keys, tokens and signing secrets masked by default with Copy and Reveal actions, and put Rotate or Regenerate next to a sentence that says what breaks when the old value stops working.

- Why: Secrets on screen leak through screenshots and screen sharing; and rotating a secret silently breaks every client that still uses the old one.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The integrations area displays any API key, access token, webhook signing secret or password.
- Exceptions: A newly created secret may be shown once in full, with a notice that it will not be shown again. Only the rotation warning was observed; masking was not, and two reference portals show secrets in plain text, which this rule treats as a defect.
- Do: 'API key ******** [Copy] [Reveal]'; section 'Refresh token' with 'Rotating invalidates the current token. Update every connected instance with the new one.' and a 'Rotate token' button that asks for confirmation.
- Don't: A webhook signing secret or API key printed in plain text in a paragraph, with a bare 'Regenerate' button and no warning.
- Check (static): Search the integrations and API pages for fields that render secrets. Confirm each renders masked by default, offers copy and reveal, and that every rotate or regenerate action has adjacent consequence text and a confirmation step.
- Check (live): Open each page that holds a key or secret, confirm no secret is readable without clicking Reveal, then click Rotate on a test credential and confirm a dialog states the consequence before anything changes.

### INT-011 — Integration placement follows what it adds

**Rule:** Give an integration its own navigation group only when it brings its own day-to-day screens; keep integrations that only feed data or identity under settings, in a connections group, or under the product area they serve.

- Why: Navigation is for daily work; a data feed that people configure once would add a permanent menu item nobody uses, while an app with its own work screens would be buried if it lived only in settings.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Deciding where a new integration appears in the navigation.
- Exceptions: The three reference portals place integrations differently (injected nav group, settings only, product-scoped); this rule is the condition that explains all three, but it is inferred from that split, not documented. When an integration has its own nav group, the global settings list should still list it and link to its own Settings item.
- Do: A third-party reviews app adds a nav group 'Reviews' with items Reviews, Analytics, Settings; a store connector that only imports orders lives at Settings > Connections > Integrations; a login provider lives under the access product's Integrations item.
- Don't: A top-level menu item for an order-import connector that is configured once and then only produces log rows.
- Check (static): For each integration, list its screens. If it has screens for daily work, confirm it has a nav group that includes a Settings item and that the global settings list of integrations links to it. If it has only configuration and logs, confirm it has no top-level nav item and sits under settings or its product area.
- Check (live): Install one work-surface integration and one data-feed integration in a test account; confirm only the first adds a navigation group, and both are reachable from the settings list of integrations.

### INT-012 — Disconnect is secondary, confirmed and recorded

**Rule:** Offer disconnect or uninstall as a secondary row or overflow action, confirm it in a dialog that names the connection and states what stops and what data is kept or deleted, and keep a list of removed integrations.

- Why: Disconnecting stops imports, write-back or logins at once; a confirmation that states the consequence prevents accidental outages, and a removed-list lets people reconnect or audit later.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: A connection can be removed by the user.
- Exceptions: Destructive bulk actions on data the integration imported (for example 'Delete all unshipped orders') are separate from disconnecting and need their own confirmation; they must not share a button or dialog with Remove. The confirmation dialogs themselves were not opened in the reference portals; the dialog content follows documented destructive-modal guidance.
- Do: Row action 'Remove integration' opens 'Remove store connection? Orders will stop importing and tracking will no longer be sent back. Imported orders stay in your account.' with buttons [Cancel] [Remove integration] (critical style); the list has tabs Installed / Uninstalled.
- Don't: A primary-styled 'Disconnect' button at the top of the detail page that removes the connection on one click with an 'Are you sure? OK' dialog.
- Check (static): Find every disconnect, remove or uninstall action. Confirm it is styled as secondary or critical (never primary), lives in a row action or overflow menu, opens a confirmation whose primary button repeats the verb and whose text names the connection and its consequences, and that removed connections remain listed in a separate view.
- Check (live): On a test connection, click remove; confirm a dialog names the connection and the consequence, Cancel leaves everything unchanged, and confirming moves the connection to an uninstalled or removed view rather than erasing all trace of it.

## branding

### BRD-001 — One brand source for every customer surface

**Rule:** Keep logo, favicon, colours, store name and social links in one brand page, and make every customer-facing surface (emails, tracking page, portals) read from it.

- Why: When each surface has its own logo and colour fields, they drift apart and the merchant has to repeat every brand change in several places.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The product sends or hosts two or more things the end customer sees (emails, a tracking or status page, a returns or self-service portal, documents).
- Exceptions: A product whose only customer-facing output is one hosted page (for example a custom error page) can keep its look inside that page's editor.
- Do: Settings > Brand holds logo, colours and social links. The email editor and the tracking page editor show a line 'Logo and colours come from Brand' with a link to it.
- Don't: A returns portal tab with its own logo upload and its own header and accent colours, next to a brand page that already holds a logo and colours.
- Check (static): List every field that sets a logo, favicon, colour or social link. Each must exist in exactly one place, the brand page; any surface editor that repeats one of them fails.
- Check (live): Change the primary colour on the brand page and save. Open the preview of each customer surface (email, tracking page, portal); every one must show the new colour without any further edit.

### BRD-002 — Say where brand assets appear

**Rule:** On the brand page, list the customer surfaces or channels that use these assets, and say when a surface renders them differently.

- Why: The merchant cannot judge the effect of a logo or colour change unless they know which customer touchpoints it reaches.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any brand page or any shared content block (for example a notice banner) that is reused on more than one customer surface.
- Exceptions: None known.
- Do: Under the page title: 'Used on: order emails, tracking page, returns portal.' A shared notice block says 'Shown on tracking page, emails and returns portal.'
- Don't: A brand page with only a 'Logo' field and no word on where the logo will be shown.
- Check (static): Read the brand page spec or screenshot. It must name every surface that consumes the assets; compare that list with the actual list of customer surfaces in the product.
- Check (live): Open the brand page and each shared block. Visible text (not a tooltip) must name the surfaces; follow each named surface and confirm it really uses the asset.

### BRD-003 — Rendered preview with sample data

**Rule:** Give every editable customer-facing template a rendered preview with realistic sample data, reachable from the editor in one click.

- Why: Templates mix brand assets, variables and optional blocks, and only the rendered result shows broken layout, empty variables or wrong colours before customers see them.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Email templates, tracking or status pages, customer portals, printable documents (packing slips, invoices), hosted error pages.
- Exceptions: Plain-text single-line content (a subject line alone) can rely on its field value; a downloadable document can preview as a sample PDF if an inline render is not possible.
- Do: Email editor with the form on the left and a live rendered preview on the right, using a sample order; subject line shown above the preview.
- Don't: An email editor whose only way to see the result is to send a test email, or a preview that sits two levels deeper on a separate route and saves settings when opened.
- Check (static): For each customer-facing template in the spec, find its preview. Fail if there is none, if it uses placeholder tokens instead of sample values, or if it needs more than one click from the editor.
- Check (live): Open each template editor, change a text field without saving, and open the preview. It must render the unsaved change with sample data, and the settings audit log or network panel must show no write caused by opening the preview.

### BRD-004 — Send a test message

**Rule:** Next to every customer email template, offer 'Send test' to an address the merchant chooses, using the current unsaved content.

- Why: Email clients render HTML differently from the admin preview, so a real message in a real inbox is the final check.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any template that is delivered as an email or SMS to the end customer.
- Exceptions: Messages the product cannot send outside a live event (for example a carrier-generated message) may say so instead of offering a test.
- Do: Header action 'Send test'; a small dialog with the recipient pre-filled with the signed-in user's address, editable.
- Don't: A 'Send test email' button that stays disabled with no hint that an address must be typed first.
- Check (static): For each customer email template, confirm a test-send action exists, that the recipient is editable, and that the disabled state has a visible reason.
- Check (live): Edit an email template, click the test action, send to your own inbox, and confirm the received message matches the preview and includes the unsaved change.

### BRD-005 — Customer emails listed by lifecycle stage

**Rule:** List customer messages grouped by the stage of the customer journey that triggers them, and give each row its trigger in one line and its on/off state.

- Why: Merchants think in terms of what the customer is going through (ordered, shipped, delivered, returned), and the trigger line answers 'when does this go out?' without opening the template.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The product sends three or more automatic messages to end customers.
- Exceptions: A product with one or two messages can show them as cards without groups.
- Do: Group 'Delivery': 'Shipped - sent when a label is created' [on], 'Out for delivery - sent when the carrier reports the last mile' [off]. Clicking the name opens the editor.
- Don't: An alphabetical list of template names with no trigger, or checkboxes whose accessible name is the same 'Edit template' text on every row.
- Check (static): Inspect the message list. Each row needs a name, a one-line trigger ('Sent when ...'), an on/off state and a link to its editor; rows are grouped by journey stage; every control has a unique accessible name.
- Check (live): Open the list with a screen reader or accessibility inspector. Each on/off control must announce the message name. Toggle one message off and confirm the state persists after reload.

### BRD-006 — Sender identity and deliverability in one place

**Rule:** Show the sender name and address with the sending domain's authentication status, the exact records to fix it, and the fallback sender used until it is fixed.

- Why: Unauthenticated sender domains send customer emails to spam; the merchant must see the problem and its fix where they set the sender.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The product sends email to end customers from an address or domain the merchant supplies.
- Exceptions: If the product always sends from its own domain and the merchant can only set a display name, show only the display name and the reply-to address.
- Do: Sender card: 'From: Store name <hello@brand.example>' with a status badge 'Domain not verified', a 'View DNS records' link, and 'Until verified, emails go out from a shared address.'
- Don't: A From email field with an SPF hint repeated under it twice, and no status saying whether the domain is actually authenticated.
- Check (static): Find every place where a sender address can be set. Each must show an authentication status, a link or panel with the required DNS records, and the fallback sender text.
- Check (live): Enter a sender address on an unverified domain. A visible warning status must appear with the required records; after adding the records, the status must change without contacting support.

### BRD-007 — Colour fields with role, swatch and hex

**Rule:** Name each brand colour by its role, pair a swatch picker with an editable hex field, and state where that role is used.

- Why: A role name ('Text', 'Links', 'Background') tells the merchant what will change, and the hex field lets them paste exact brand values.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any setting that changes a colour on a customer-facing surface.
- Exceptions: A single accent colour can skip the role name if the page already says where it appears.
- Do: 'Primary - buttons and headings' [swatch] [#1A3A5F] [Reset]; 'Contrasting - text on primary' [swatch] [#FFFFFF]. Warn when the pair fails a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
- Don't: 'Colour 1', 'Colour 2' swatches with no hex field, or a hex field whose accessible name is the placeholder '#000000'.
- Check (static): For every colour setting, check for a role label, a swatch, an editable hex text input whose accessible name contains the role (not a placeholder such as '#000000'), and a line saying where the role is used.
- Check (live): Type a valid hex value; the swatch must update. Pick a colour with the swatch; the hex field must update. Type an invalid value such as '#12'; a field-level error must appear and Save must not store it.

### BRD-008 — Upload fields state formats, size and current file

**Rule:** Next to every image upload, show the current image as a thumbnail, the accepted formats and the recommended size, with Replace and Remove actions.

- Why: Logos are reused at many sizes; saying the formats and minimum size up front avoids blurry or cropped output and failed uploads.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Logo, square logo, favicon, cover, promotion and any other image the end customer will see.
- Exceptions: None known.
- Do: 'Square logo - may be cropped into a circle. SVG, PNG or JPG, at least 512x512 px.' [thumbnail] [Change] [Remove].
- Don't: A bare 'Choose file' button with no thumbnail of the logo in use and no size guidance.
- Check (static): For each image input in the spec, verify thumbnail, format list, recommended pixel size, and Replace/Remove actions; also a note when the image may be cropped.
- Check (live): Upload a valid image; the thumbnail must show the new file. Click Remove; the thumbnail must disappear. Upload a file in an unsupported format; it must be rejected with a field error that names the allowed formats.

### BRD-009 — Reset to default and visible fallback

**Rule:** Give every brand value and template a 'Reset to default' action, and state what the customer sees when the value is empty or the feature is off.

- Why: Merchants experiment with customer-facing looks; a one-click way back, and knowing the fallback, makes those changes safe.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Colours, logos, template content and on/off choices for customer surfaces.
- Exceptions: Free-text fields with no product default (slogan, social links) need only Remove, not Reset.
- Do: 'If no template is selected, customers see the carrier's standard tracking page.' Each colour row ends with a 'Reset Primary to default' icon button; a 'Reset to default' for the whole editor sits in the save bar, and a reset only stages the change until Save.
- Don't: Clearing the logo field with no indication of what will appear in emails instead.
- Check (static): For every brand value and template, check for a reset or remove action with a specific accessible name, and for a sentence describing the empty or off state.
- Check (live): Change a colour and a template block, then use Reset. The values must return to defaults, and the preview must match. Turn a customer surface off and confirm the page states what replaces it.

### BRD-010 — Customer messages apart from staff alerts

**Rule:** Keep messages sent to end customers in their own list, separate from alerts sent to staff, partners or webhooks.

- Why: Editing a customer email has brand and legal impact; mixing it with internal alerts invites changing the wrong thing.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The product sends both customer-facing messages and internal notifications.
- Exceptions: If internal alerts are only account alerts about the product itself (billing, outages), they belong in account or profile settings, not next to customer messages at all.
- Do: Notifications page with three links: 'Customer notifications', 'Staff notifications', 'Webhooks'.
- Don't: One list where 'Order confirmation' (to customer) sits between 'New order alert' (to staff) and 'Webhook failed'.
- Check (static): List every message template and its recipient type. Fail if a single list mixes end-customer recipients with staff or system recipients.
- Check (live): Open the customer message list and confirm every entry is received by the end customer; open each internal list and confirm none is.

### BRD-011 — Optional blocks behind an enable checkbox

**Rule:** In a customer template editor, show each optional content block (notice, contact, promotion, footer) as a section with an 'Enable' checkbox that reveals its fields, and say that empty fields are hidden from the customer.

- Why: Merchants build a template by turning blocks on and off; the checkbox makes the template's structure readable and blank blocks never leak to customers.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Form-based template editors with a fixed set of optional sections.
- Exceptions: Code-based template editors (raw HTML or a template language) control blocks in code instead.
- Do: 'Promotion block' heading, one-line purpose, [ ] Enable promotion block; when checked, image and link fields appear. Note: 'Fields left blank are not shown.'
- Don't: All optional fields always visible with no way to tell whether the block will appear to customers.
- Check (static): In each template editor spec, every optional section has a heading, a purpose line, an enable checkbox and a statement on blank fields.
- Check (live): Toggle each enable checkbox; its fields must appear and disappear, and the preview must add and remove the block.

## states

### STA-001 — Empty state says why and offers the one action that fills it

**Rule:** When a list or section has no items yet, replace the empty table with a heading that says what will appear here, one sentence on what it is for, and one primary action that creates the first item.

- Why: A bare empty table looks like a loading or permission failure; naming the content and the action that fills it turns the first visit into the first step of the job.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: A list, table or section has zero items because nothing has been created or received yet.
- Exceptions: Zero results caused by a search or filter use the no-match state (IDX-011); a feature that needs setup or a plan before it can hold items uses its onboarding empty state (ONB-007) or the locked state (STA-005). Controls that act on rows (sort, view tabs, bulk actions) are disabled while the list is empty, not removed.
- Do: Heading 'Create your first API token', one line on what tokens do, button 'Create token', link 'Learn more'; the page's own 'Create' button stays in the title bar.
- Don't: An empty grid with column headers and 'Showing 0-0 of 0' as the only text, or an empty state with three competing buttons.
- Check (static): For every list component, find the zero-items branch; verify it renders a heading or sentence naming the missing content, exactly one primary action that creates an item, at most one secondary link, and that row-level controls are disabled (not hidden) in that branch.
- Check (live): Open each list on a fresh account or with all items deleted; confirm the explanatory text and a single primary create action are visible without scrolling, and that clicking it opens the create flow.

### STA-002 — Empty state sized to its container

**Rule:** Use a full empty-state block (optional illustration, heading, text, action) when a whole page is empty, and a compact message of at most two lines, with no illustration and at most one inline action, when only a sub-table, tab panel or section inside a larger page is empty.

- Why: A page-sized illustration inside a small settings table pushes real controls off screen, while a one-line hint on an otherwise empty page leaves users unsure what the page is for.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Choosing the visual weight of an empty state.
- Exceptions: A primary work-area list that is empty on first use gets the full block even if it sits inside tabs, because it is the main content of the page.
- Do: Whole campaigns page empty: heading, two-line explanation, 'Create campaign', 'Learn more'. Tags table inside a settings page empty: one row reading 'No tags yet. Click Add new to create your first tag.'
- Don't: A 300px illustration inside a settings card that holds a two-column table, or a top-level list page whose only content is 'No records.'
- Check (static): List every empty-state instance with its container (page main vs card/section/tab panel); verify page-level instances use the full block and nested instances render at most two lines of text, no illustration and at most one inline action.
- Check (live): Empty one page-level list and one nested table; at 1440px confirm the nested empty state has no illustration and is no taller than two lines of body text, and the page-level one shows a heading and a primary action in the main area.

### STA-003 — Loading placeholders in place and announced

**Rule:** While data loads, show a placeholder exactly where the value or content will appear (ellipsis, skeleton line or small spinner) and expose it to assistive technology as a status, instead of a blank area, a page-wide blocker or a provisional zero.

- Why: An in-place placeholder keeps the layout stable and tells users which part is still coming; a provisional 0 is read as a real value and a blank region is read as broken.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Any page or region whose content arrives asynchronously, including counters in tabs, metric tiles, table bodies and side panels, and any user-started job whose result appears on the page.
- Exceptions: A route change may use one thin top progress bar for the page shell; the regions inside still follow this rule. Home blocks additionally load independently (HOM-010). A short confirmation action (Save, Delete) may show progress on its own button (disabled with a spinner) instead of in the content.
- Do: Tab counters read 'Printed …' until counted; metric links read 'Invocations Loading...' with a status role; a table shows skeleton rows of the final height.
- Don't: Counters that show 0 and then jump to 12, a full-screen spinner over the whole admin, or an empty main area with no indication that anything is loading.
- Check (static): For each async component, verify a loading branch renders a placeholder in the same slot with role="status" or aria-busy="true" on the region, and that numeric fields are null (not 0) until the response arrives.
- Check (live): Throttle the network to Slow 3G and reload list, detail and home pages; confirm every pending region shows a placeholder in place, no counter shows 0 before its real value, and a screen reader or the accessibility tree reports a loading status.

### STA-004 — A failed region says so and offers retry

**Rule:** When a page or region fails to load, replace it with a short message that says what could not be loaded and a Retry action, and keep the rest of the page usable.

- Why: A blank region after a failure cannot be told apart from an empty or still-loading one, so users wait, reload the whole app or conclude they have no data.
- Confidence: low (source inferred; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: A request for page or region content fails or times out.
- Exceptions: Optional dashboard widgets may collapse to a one-line message inside the widget. Unknown URLs use the not-found page (STA-006). Failures of a user-submitted form are shown as field errors and a form-level message, not as a region error. Failures that block all work (session expired, service down) use one page-level banner instead of one message per region.
- Do: Videos list area: 'Videos could not be loaded.' with a 'Retry' button; the sidebar, title and other cards stay interactive.
- Don't: The main area stays blank after 15 seconds with no message, no spinner and no empty state.
- Check (static): For each data-fetching component, verify there is an error branch distinct from the empty and loading branches, that it renders a message naming the content and a retry handler that refetches only that region, and that an error boundary wraps each independent region.
- Check (live): Block one API endpoint in devtools (request blocking) and reload; confirm the affected region shows the error message and Retry within the request timeout, other regions render normally, and Retry recovers after unblocking.

### STA-005 — Locked features stay visible with the requirement and the unlock path

**Rule:** When a feature or option is unavailable because of the plan, an entitlement or another setting, keep it visible but disabled, state in visible text what is required, and offer the action that unlocks it next to it.

- Why: Hidden features cannot be discovered or bought, and a feature that looks available but fails after a click wastes the attempt; stating the requirement up front lets users decide to upgrade or change the blocking setting.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: A control, tab or whole section exists in the product but the current account cannot use it.
- Exceptions: When a whole tab or page is locked, replace its content with the requirement and an unlock action instead of disabling every control; still keep the tab in navigation. Explanation copy for a single disabled control follows HLP-006. Role-based restrictions are not covered here (see open questions).
- Do: Disabled switch labelled with its plan ('Pro plan') beside an 'Upgrade plan' button; a locked tab whose content names the required plan and offers 'Upgrade plan' and 'Contact sales'.
- Don't: An enabled control that opens a 'No access' dialog only after the click, or a locked tab whose content is a sentence about a paid plan with no upgrade or contact action.
- Check (static): For every entitlement or dependency check in the UI code, verify the gated control renders in a disabled state (not omitted), that adjacent visible text names the requirement, and that an unlock action (upgrade link, link to the blocking setting) is rendered; verify no gated action is reachable only to fail server-side.
- Check (live): Use an account on the lowest plan; open each page with plan-gated features and confirm each is visible, disabled, explained in text and paired with an unlock action; click every enabled control and confirm none returns an entitlement or access error.

### STA-006 — Not-found page inside the shell with a way forward

**Rule:** Render an unknown or removed URL as a not-found page inside the normal navigation shell, with a plain heading that the page does not exist and at least one way forward (search, a home or parent link).

- Why: Keeping the shell lets users continue from where they are; a heading plus a next step turns a dead link into a one-click detour instead of a reason to log out and back in.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: A route does not match, or an object id in the URL no longer exists or is outside the current scope.
- Exceptions: A deleted object reached from a stale link may say it was deleted and link to its list instead of the generic text.
- Do: Sidebar and search visible; heading 'There's no page at this address'; text 'Check the URL, or search for what you need' with search focused or linked; link back to the area's overview.
- Don't: A bare server 404 page without the app chrome, or a blank main area with no heading.
- Check (static): In the router, verify a catch-all route and object-not-found responses render a component inside the authenticated layout, with an h1 or h2 stating the page does not exist and at least one link or control for search or home.
- Check (live): Visit an invalid path and an invalid object id in each top-level area; confirm the sidebar stays visible, the heading explains the page is missing, and a search or home link works.

## feedback

### FDB-001 — One channel per kind of event

**Rule:** Pick the feedback channel from the event, not from taste - toast for the outcome of the user's own action, inline error for an invalid field, banner for an ongoing status or required action, modal for a decision that must be made before continuing, status text for progress and current state.

- Why: Each channel promises a different lifetime and urgency; when the mapping is fixed, users learn where to look and nothing important disappears with a timeout or blocks work that did not need blocking.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Designing any message the product shows in response to an action, a validation, a background process or a state change.
- Exceptions: One-time announcements for a redesigned area may use a dismissible dialog (see onboarding rules). Field-level help that is not an error stays a description, not a feedback channel.
- Do: Save succeeds: toast 'Rule saved'. Weight empty: red text under the field 'Enter a weight'. Integration token expired: section banner with 'Reconnect'. Delete: modal 'Delete 3 rules?' with 'Delete' and 'Cancel'. Import running: status text 'Importing 120 of 400'.
- Don't: A modal 'Settings saved' with an OK button; a toast 'Weight is required' after Save; a banner that says 'Saving...'.
- Check (static): Build the event inventory of the spec (success, field invalid, request failed, background failure, blocked state, destructive confirm, in progress) and confirm each maps to exactly one channel from the table; grep the code for modal/dialog opens in success handlers and for toast calls inside field validators, expect none.
- Check (live): Trigger one event of each kind (save a valid form, submit an empty required field, start a long job, open a delete action) and read the accessibility tree each time - success lands in the toast region, the invalid field gets aria-invalid with its message, the job shows role=status text in place, and only the delete opens role=dialog or alertdialog.

### FDB-002 — Lasting conditions never live only in a toast

**Rule:** Report any condition that stays true after the moment passes (feature locked, permission or plan missing, integration broken, required setup step) in persistent text at the place it affects, not only in a toast.

- Why: A toast vanishes after a few seconds and is easy to miss on small screens; a blocked user who missed it has no way to learn why the control does nothing.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The user's next attempt would fail for the same reason (state, plan, role, missing setup), or the problem persists until someone acts.
- Exceptions: A toast may announce the condition at the moment it is first detected, as long as the same text also stays in place afterwards.
- Do: A card that replaces its controls with 'This feature needs a paid plan' and an 'Upgrade plan' button, visible on every visit.
- Don't: A card whose controls look normal and only a corner toast 'No access' appears when the page opens.
- Check (static): For every disabled, locked or blocked state in the spec, find persistent in-page text or a banner tied to the affected section; flag any toast call whose message describes a plan, permission, entitlement or configuration problem with no matching in-place element.
- Check (live): Open a locked or unconfigured feature at 1440 px and at 390 px, wait 10 seconds, then read the accessibility tree; the reason must still be present as text inside main next to the affected control, not only inside the toast region.

### FDB-003 — Field errors sit under the field

**Rule:** Show a validation error as text directly below the field it concerns, mark the field invalid, and state length, format or range limits before the user types.

- Why: The user has to fix the field, so the message must be where their eyes and focus are; stating limits up front prevents most errors from happening at all.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl observed, cloudflare documented)
- Applies when: Any input that the client or server can reject.
- Exceptions: Errors that involve several fields together (dates out of order, conflicting rules) go next to the group, plus a short summary at the top of a long form that links to each field.
- Do: Field 'Days to import' with helper 'Between 1 and 30' under it; after entering 45, red text 'Enter a number from 1 to 30' replaces the helper and the field is outlined.
- Don't: A toast 'Invalid input' after Save with no indication of which of twelve fields is wrong.
- Check (static): Every form field component renders an error slot below the input wired with aria-describedby and sets aria-invalid when the error is present; inputs with limits render the limit as helper text before any error.
- Check (live): Before typing, read the accessible description of every field that has a length, format or range limit and confirm it states the limit; then submit the form with one invalid value and confirm the field has aria-invalid=true, its accessible description contains the error text, the error element renders directly below that input, and the error is not shown only in a toast.

### FDB-004 — Background failures stay on the object and in a log

**Rule:** When a job or sync that runs without the user (import, publish, webhook, scheduled task) fails, record it as a persistent error on the affected object with a count, and as a row in a log with time and outcome.

- Why: Nobody is watching when a background job fails, so a transient message would be lost; a count on the object and a log row let the user find, understand and retry the failure later.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Work that the system does on a schedule or on events from another system.
- Exceptions: When the failure blocks the whole integration (expired credentials, revoked access), also show a banner with the fix action (see FDB-002).
- Do: Product page card 'Sales channels' with '1 channel error' that opens the reason; Logs > Imports row '10:20, 0 imported, Error: order has no line items'.
- Don't: A toast 'Import failed' shown to whoever happens to be online, with no log entry.
- Check (static): For each background job in the spec, find the persisted failure record (log table with time, outcome and reason) and the UI element that shows a failure count on the affected object; flag jobs whose failure path only emits a notification.
- Check (live): Force one background job to fail (bad record or revoked test credentials), reload the app, and confirm the affected object shows an error count and the log lists a row with timestamp, outcome and reason.

### FDB-007 — Modals only for decisions that must come first

**Rule:** Open a modal only when the user must decide or confirm something before the action can proceed, name its primary button after the action, and never open one modal from another.

- Why: A modal stops all other work; spending it on news or confirmations of success teaches users to dismiss modals without reading, including the destructive ones.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Destructive or irreversible actions, choices that change what happens next, and short inputs needed to finish an action (a name for a new view).
- Exceptions: A one-time welcome or what's-new dialog for a redesigned area is allowed once per user and must be dismissible. Large forms never go in a modal; use a page.
- Do: Dialog 'Delete 3 shipping rules? This can't be undone.' with a red 'Delete rules' button and 'Cancel'.
- Don't: Dialog 'Changes saved successfully' with an OK button; a confirm dialog that opens a second dialog 'Are you sure?'.
- Check (static): List every dialog in the spec or code; each one is opened only from a user action that needs a decision or input, has a primary button whose label is a verb from the action (not OK or Yes), and no dialog component renders another dialog trigger that opens while it is open.
- Check (live): On test data, save an edited form and start a delete; the save opens no role=dialog or alertdialog, the delete opens exactly one, its primary button name contains the action verb (not OK or Yes), and activating that button closes the dialog without opening a second one.

### FDB-008 — Live regions exist before messages arrive

**Rule:** Mount the toast region and the status and alert live regions once at the app root when the shell loads, and use them to announce content that finishes loading after navigation.

- Why: Screen readers only announce changes to live regions that already exist in the page; a region created together with its message is often read late or not at all.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Single-page apps where content and messages change without a full page load.
- Exceptions: Purely static pages with no async content or feedback need no live regions.
- Do: Shell renders <section aria-label='Notifications'> for toasts and an empty role=status node; after route change it writes 'Orders loaded' into the status node.
- Don't: A toast library that appends a new aria-live element to the body only when the first toast fires.
- Check (static): The root layout renders one named toast region and one role=status (and, if used, one role=alert) element unconditionally; feature code sends messages through them instead of creating new aria-live nodes.
- Check (live): Load any page and, before acting, read the accessibility tree - the named toast region and an empty status region are already present; navigate to another page with async data and confirm a status or alert announcement appears once the content is ready.

### FDB-009 — Toasts with actions stay reachable

**Rule:** When a toast carries an action (Undo, Retry, View), let keyboard users jump into the toast region with a shortcut named in the region's label, and keep the toast visible for at least 10 seconds with the timer paused on hover and focus, until the user acts or dismisses it.

- Why: An Undo that disappears in four seconds or cannot be reached by keyboard is not a real undo; keyboard and screen-reader users need a way into the toast before it goes.
- Confidence: low (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any toast that contains a button or link.
- Exceptions: Plain confirmation toasts without an action may auto-dismiss after a few seconds.
- Do: Toast 'Rule deleted' with 'Undo'; the region is named 'Notifications alt+T', pressing Alt+T moves focus to it, and hover or focus pauses the timer.
- Don't: An 'Undo' toast that vanishes after 3 seconds and can only be reached with the mouse.
- Check (static): The toast region's accessible name includes its shortcut and a global key handler for that shortcut moves focus into the region; every toast call with an action sets a duration of at least 10000 ms or no auto-dismiss, and the toast component pauses its timer on mouseenter and focusin.
- Check (live): Trigger an action that produces a toast with Undo or Retry and, without the mouse, press the shortcut named in the region's label; focus must land on the toast action, the toast must still be present 10 seconds after it appeared, and it must stay while focused past its normal duration.

## microcopy

### MCP-001 — Buttons start with a verb and name the object

**Rule:** Label every action button with an imperative verb followed by the object it acts on, and keep a bare verb only when the object is unambiguous from the surrounding card or dialog.

- Why: A verb tells users the button does something, and the object tells them to what; a list of verb + object buttons can be scanned without reading the page around it.
- Confidence: medium (source documented; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Primary and secondary buttons on pages, cards, toolbars and dialogs.
- Exceptions: Standard short commands whose object is the whole form or dialog (Save, Cancel, Close, Export, Import) may stay a bare verb, as may Edit and Apply inside a card or dialog that names its object; toggles that show a state use the state or setting name instead.
- Do: "Add product", "Create rule", "Rotate token", "Print label".
- Don't: "New", "Add new", "OK", "Go", "Submit" on a page with several objects.
- Check (static): Extract all button labels from the component tree or string catalog; flag any whose first word is not a verb from the product's verb list, and any lone verb outside the allowed set (Save, Cancel, Close, Export, Import, Edit, Apply).
- Check (live): Dump the accessibility tree of each index and detail page; every role=button with visible text must start with a verb from the verb list, and the primary button of an index page must contain the singular of the H1 noun (H1 "Products", button "Add product") unless it is on the allowed bare-verb list.

### MCP-002 — Sentence case for all interface text

**Rule:** Write menu items, page titles, headings, tabs, column headers, buttons and section labels in sentence case, capitalising only the first word and proper names, and never store labels in ALL CAPS.

- Why: One casing rule removes a whole class of inconsistency; mixed Title Case and sentence case on one screen looks unfinished, and ALL CAPS text is slower to read and is spelled out letter by letter by some screen readers.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl observed, cloudflare documented)
- Applies when: All visible labels and headings in the product.
- Exceptions: Proper product or feature names and acronyms keep their own capitalisation (API, DNS). A small uppercase eyebrow style may be applied with CSS text-transform as long as the source string stays in sentence case.
- Do: "Shipping and delivery", "Edge certificates", "Create purchase order", column "Expires on".
- Don't: "Posture Findings" beside "Cloud & SaaS findings"; heading "Active Subscriptions"; a hard-coded "ORDER MANAGEMENT" string.
- Check (static): Lint the string catalog; flag strings with two or more capitalised words that are not in the proper-name allowlist, and strings that are entirely uppercase.
- Check (live): On each page, read element.textContent (the source string, before CSS text-transform) of every heading, tab, columnheader, button and nav link; report any label with two or more capitalised words not in the proper-name allowlist, and any label that is entirely uppercase in the source.

### MCP-003 — Destinations are nouns, commands are verbs

**Rule:** In every menu (sidebar, user menu, overflow menu), word items that open a page as nouns and items that perform an action as verbs, so the wording tells users what will happen on click.

- Why: Users predict the result of a click from its grammar; a noun promises a place, a verb promises a change, and mixing them misleads.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Sidebar navigation, tabs, user and account menus, overflow menus that mix links and actions.
- Exceptions: Overflow menus that only hold actions on one object are all verbs. A nav item for a single dominant task may use the task noun ("Search") rather than the verb.
- Do: Sidebar "Orders", "Pickups"; user menu "Profile", "Billing", "Log out".
- Don't: Sidebar "Manage users", "View reports"; user menu "Go to billing" next to "Profile".
- Check (static): In nav and menu definitions, flag items with an href whose label starts with a verb, and items with an onClick action (no href) whose label does not start with a verb.
- Check (live): Open each menu; for every menuitem or link, read whether it carries an href; items with an href must not start with a verb, items without an href must start with a verb from the verb list.

### MCP-004 — Short button labels without filler

**Rule:** Keep button labels to one to three words, verb first, with no articles, no "new", no "now" and no explanatory clause; put any explanation in helper text next to the button.

- Why: Short labels fit in toolbars and narrow screens and are read at a glance; filler words push the object out of view and make labels inconsistent.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: All buttons and menu commands.
- Exceptions: A qualifier is allowed when two buttons on the same screen would otherwise collide ("Create custom rule" next to "Create rate limiting rule").
- Do: "Add rule", "Test connection", "Import orders", "Add identity provider".
- Don't: "Add a new rule", "Run rules now", "Test to ensure it works", "Click here to import".
- Check (static): Flag button strings longer than three words unless listed as a collision qualifier, and strings containing the whole words "a", "an", "the", "new", "now", "here" or "please".
- Check (live): On each page, list button accessible names (visible text, not aria-label extensions added for MCP-005); report any over three words or containing the filler words above as whole words.

### MCP-005 — Repeated buttons name their object

**Rule:** When the same action appears on several rows or cards, include the object in the accessible name (visible or via aria-label) so each instance is unique.

- Why: A screen-reader or voice user who hears "Pin, Pin, Pin" or "Add new" ten times cannot tell which item each button affects; automation and tests cannot target them either.
- Confidence: low (source inferred; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Row actions in tables and lists, card actions repeated across a grid, per-item pin/star/remove buttons.
- Exceptions: The visible label may stay short ("Pin") if the accessible name adds the object ("Pin Invoices").
- Do: Visible "Remove", accessible name "Remove shipping method Standard"; "Sort by order date".
- Don't: Thirty buttons all named "Pin"; every card with an "Add new" button.
- Check (static): In list and table row templates, check that action buttons receive an aria-label or visually hidden text interpolating the row's name; lint for duplicate accessible names within one page.
- Check (live): Dump the accessibility tree per page; group buttons by accessible name; any name repeated more than once that is not a global control (Close, Save) is a failure.

### MCP-006 — One verb per kind of action

**Rule:** Define a product-wide verb list (for example "Add" to put an existing or simple item into a list, "Create" to build a new configured object, "Remove" to take out of a list, "Delete" to destroy) and use each verb only for its meaning.

- Why: When the same act is called "Add new", "Add a new rule" and "Create rule" on neighbouring pages, users wonder whether they are different operations; a fixed verb list makes behaviour predictable.
- Confidence: low (source inferred; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any product with more than one create or remove flow.
- Exceptions: Domain verbs with a fixed meaning for the user (Print, Deploy, Rotate, Purge) are kept and added to the list rather than replaced by a generic verb.
- Do: Every list uses "Add <item>"; every configurable object uses "Create <object>"; Remove takes out of a list, Delete destroys.
- Don't: "Add new" on one rules page, "Create rule" on the next, "Delete" used for unlinking a member.
- Check (static): Keep the verb list in the string catalog or a lint config; grep button labels and flag verbs not on the list and the same object noun paired with two different create verbs.
- Check (live): Collect every create-type button across index pages; for each object noun, confirm only one verb is used.

### MCP-007 — One term per concept, one concept per term

**Rule:** Keep a glossary and use the same term for a concept in the menu, page title, breadcrumbs, buttons, notifications and shortcuts, matching singular and plural, and never reuse one term for two different concepts.

- Why: Different words for the same thing ("Quotes" in the menu, "Quote" as the title) and the same word for different things ("Notifications" for toasts and for a settings tab) make users doubt they are in the right place.
- Confidence: low (source inferred; shopify absent, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Every user-facing noun for an object, area or feature.
- Exceptions: After a rename, the old term may survive only as a search alias, never as a visible label.
- Do: Menu "Quotes", title "Quotes", breadcrumb "Quotes"; toasts announced as "Status messages", alert rules under "Notifications".
- Don't: Menu "Quotes", page title "Quote"; "Notifications" meaning both toasts and email alerts.
- Check (static): Maintain a glossary file; derive nav labels, page titles and shortcut labels from the same keys; flag string-catalog entries that use a glossary synonym or differ only by plural from the canonical term.
- Check (live): For each nav item, compare its label with the H1, breadcrumb and tab title of the target page; flag any mismatch, including singular vs plural; flag any accessible name used both for a landmark or live region and for a nav link or tab that leads to a different page.

### MCP-008 — One spelling variant across the product
